newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says seizes 5,500 T imported sugar.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says seizes 5,500 T imported sugar.

text.p: The Philippines, determined to protect its sugarcane farms from illegal imports flooding the market, seized 5,500 tonnes of imported raw sugar, the Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) said on Monday.
SRA chief Wilson Gamboa said the sugar arrived in the Port of Batangas on September 30 from Australia.
"The Bureau of Customs issued a warrant of seizure and detention on the 5,500 tonnes of raw sugar consigned undocumented to local food manufacturers," Gamboa told Reuters in a phone interview.
Gamboa said the sugar is now being held at the state-owned PNOC warehouse in Mabini, Batangas near Manila.
"We are now coordinating with the Bureau of Customs on the proper legal steps that should be taken against the buyer of the sugar," Gamboa told Reuters.
Despite abundant local supplies of sugar, traders have been wanting to import because it is cheaper.
Gamboa said local sugar farmers and millers had criticised the SRA saying imports had caused a glut in the market.
Last month, Gamboa in a bid to protect local farmers, ordered traders and millers to refrain from importing sugar up to March 1997.
Gamboa said the Philippines imported 1.23 million tonnes of sugar from September 1995 to July 1996, resulting in an excess of 423,000 tonnes.
